newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom - foreigners can't buy new local shares.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom - foreigners can't buy new local shares.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree stopping foreign companies, including Russian-registered subsidiaries, from buying new local shares of natural gas monopoly Gazprom, the head of Gazprom's securities department said he had been told on Wednesday.

"We were told it was signed, but I do not have a signed copy in my hands," Eduard Ivanov told Reuters. "If it is released in the version that I saw, foreign investors, non-residents, may not buy shares on the domestic market," he said, adding that previously-acquired shares could be held as long as the owner wished.

Ivanov said the presidential decree, which has been expected in the market and is supposed to regulate trade in Gazprom which operates separate markets for locals and foreigners, came into force upon signing.

"Subsidiaries which are residents of the Russian Federation, in which most capital is foreign and which acquired shares before the decree was released -- they will remain owners of the shares," Ivanov said, referring to locally-held Gazprom shares.

"They may not acquire any more. They may keep them as long as they want but may sell them only on the domestic market. No derivatives, none of their own shares may be issued on the basis of acquired Gazprom shares."

He said the decree would lift Gazprom's right of refusal to buy local shares on "organised exchanges" as licensed by the Federal Commission for the Securities Market but said it was not clear whether the over-the-counter type Russian Trading System, the main market for Russian shares, would be included in that list, generally considered to include only stock exchanges.
